title: Blood Pressure Trend — Hypertensive Crisis
scenario: A 58-year-old client admitted for a severe headache is placed on a nicardipine IV infusion titrated to blood pressure. The nurse monitors the blood pressure trend over the first two hours of treatment.

questions.subject: Medical-Surgical
questions.stem: Based on the blood pressure trend, how should the nurse interpret the client's response to the nicardipine infusion?

options.text: The therapy is working; blood pressure and symptoms are trending down at a controlled, gradual rate
The blood pressure is dropping too fast and the infusion should be stopped immediately
The therapy is ineffective because the blood pressure remains elevated
The rising pulse indicates the client is deteriorating

questions.rationale: The mean arterial pressure is falling gradually (about a 25% reduction over 2 hours) with improving headache and vision, which is the desired controlled response in a hypertensive emergency. An overly rapid drop risks cerebral ischemia.

questions.subject: Medical-Surgical
questions.stem: Which nursing actions are appropriate while continuing to manage this client's blood pressure trend? Select all that apply.

options.text: Continue titrating the infusion to the prescribed blood pressure parameters
Monitor for signs of cerebral hypoperfusion such as confusion or dizziness
Reassess neurologic status and headache at frequent intervals
Administer a rapid IV fluid bolus to raise the pressure
Discontinue blood pressure monitoring now that it is improving

questions.rationale: Controlled titration, frequent neuro checks, and watching for hypoperfusion are all indicated during a hypertensive emergency. Fluid boluses and stopping monitoring are inappropriate and unsafe.
